title: Composition of the Release Charge on a Car Rental Given Up
content:
The release charge withheld when a renter gives up a confirmed rental outside the rate class's free-cancellation term is the whole of the money standing on the rental's ledger at the moment the rental is given up, taken at a share of 100 percent, and the result is rounded to two decimal places.

**The money it acts on.** The money standing on the rental's ledger is every amount posted to that rental, read at the moment the rental is given up. It is the rental's own ledger and no other: a rental on the Car Rental Rate Classes carries its money on the agreement it belongs to.

**How the charge is arrived at.** The share of 100 percent is applied once to the money standing on the ledger, and the money so arrived at is rounded to two decimal places. The rounding is done once, at the end, and at no intermediate step.

**Worked through on hypothetical inputs.** Take a rental, hypothetically, given up outside its free-cancellation term with 462.375 standing on its ledger at that moment. A share of 100 percent of that money is 462.375, which rounded to two decimal places gives a release charge of 462.38. Had 200 stood on the ledger, the charge would be 200.00.
